[QUERENT] mit ai incident tracker

[SYSTEM] The [MIT AI Incident Tracker](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYgHrOzAVL1u2IQluJA7wLwjGjCgd1KNF_4Q3oolvtxOF9IE3rDSHP0824t7aqNutmp5Uuo9_uWOZ--r55XHDxbHCp1dLbhj2rMy0nXo22BPNjQQB6sTyZeaEPJ_DalZFN_sk) is an interactive tool developed by the MIT AI Risk Initiative that classifies and analyzes real-world artificial intelligence mishaps. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYgHrOzAVL1u2IQluJA7wLwjGjCgd1KNF_4Q3oolvtxOF9IE3rDSHP0824t7aqNutmp5Uuo9_uWOZ--r55XHDxbHCp1dLbhj2rMy0nXo22BPNjQQB6sTyZeaEPJ_DalZFN_sk), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHrOzAVAcXxBkPVXf7WiKunEGZxIG2NNMgARWs02O9KFJcKg8oGpwPvcOALbQt79kIKCvOLiTDSb-p76oJd6dxsiVOjSr_vn4fh1r2aiJx2cLKlIQ)]
Key Features and Overview

* Data Source: Processes and standardizes reports from the [AI Incident Database](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHrOzAVytXSna_e_8LiNaP7aJCE8Pg3CenBVPEnEskOPPbPjul7OtdSw-ZES3nA08jzQIuJ1WeF5EnYIdxABFFouPrqyMmj7eUcy5_1QjH4m6Fh8A) using automated large language model (LLM) pipelines. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHrOzAVbBlQSlGcMN7T5JtycCtyhxBu8rqTlKEIYGg_SAsZR0oR69YudvNgs6ruP6jWTmfQrX6PzCsvWQ9V1P0VdUbHS2bu1sdZPfBHuInSiRGsSTxQrHhDRKCpEnG0vJ8y2sfG1I9IAY9HR7AvWpApQZxLSS7hoQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYgHrOzAVL1u2IQluJA7wLwjGjCgd1KNF_4Q3oolvtxOF9IE3rDSHP0824t7aqNutmp5Uuo9_uWOZ--r55XHDxbHCp1dLbhj2rMy0nXo22BPNjQQB6sTyZeaEPJ_DalZFN_sk)]
* Classification Scale: Evaluates incidents using a standardized 1-5 harm severity scale and multi-dimensional taxonomies. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHrOzAV3dOprtuMGwNtCl-H3SEb8CB3pJjAZu79GQm4rXBuSU_0Gqnk05y7hqN8TqH4uG-pE0SGOwuSSchf-3i4GaqzefBF9FcRVFnNPo3rZfw8Rh6zbxctXOSCcC_jCWCP-h0B7-sutsWSuf77uQnGRskdetBf), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYgHrOzAVL1u2IQluJA7wLwjGjCgd1KNF_4Q3oolvtxOF9IE3rDSHP0824t7aqNutmp5Uuo9_uWOZ--r55XHDxbHCp1dLbhj2rMy0nXo22BPNjQQB6sTyZeaEPJ_DalZFN_sk)]
* Core Risk Domains: Categorizes incidents across areas like discrimination and toxicity, privacy and security, misinformation, malicious actors, human-computer interaction, socioeconomic and environmental impacts, and AI system safety. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYgHrOzAVL1u2IQluJA7wLwjGjCgd1KNF_4Q3oolvtxOF9IE3rDSHP0824t7aqNutmp5Uuo9_uWOZ--r55XHDxbHCp1dLbhj2rMy0nXo22BPNjQQB6sTyZeaEPJ_DalZFN_sk)]
* National Security Views: Includes specialized national security impact assessments covering physical security, information warfare, government functions, economic security, and societal stability. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHrOzAV3dOprtuMGwNtCl-H3SEb8CB3pJjAZu79GQm4rXBuSU_0Gqnk05y7hqN8TqH4uG-pE0SGOwuSSchf-3i4GaqzefBF9FcRVFnNPo3rZfw8Rh6zbxctXOSCcC_jCWCP-h0B7-sutsWSuf77uQnGRskdetBf)]
* Interactive Access: You can explore the data directly through the [MIT AI Risk Navigator](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVXxxAyswF8cBAWl6YW66eUw32rMSxnTFtYCG62HHrdO_RNJIoZ32A9BpbFWYS-vJl-CBfG0Xrd5Z_81xYyeeDFKTqh9nazFLcKbl_iBrqpcZodbsBQk8CqSI9Lw) or view broader frameworks on the [MIT AI Risk Initiative](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESTwHrOzAV52wxVoGlOq5EgufQLPRuO5uJzTvUMefC4cwWipTUlmRyI07KT-WqhDxL7YoaUkA91Jbke2P77rGPnExIKMED5xXHyIjgCp_b2OY) portal. transcript_class: CAPTURE-TIME VERBATIM RECORD — paste of the expanded Overview with its source cards
d: THE MIT AI INCIDENT TRACKER, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an interactive tool developed by the MIT AI Risk Initiative that classifies and analyzes real-world artificial intelligence mishaps'; it processes AI Incident Database reports 'using automated large language model (LLM) pipelines', rates harm on a 1–5 scale, sorts by the repository's domains, adds national-security views, and is browsable in the Risk Navigator. Six cards, all MIT's; the first card's summary says it 'classifies 1,752 real-world AI incident reports'.
reading: The innocent reading first. The Overview identifies the tracker as MIT's layer over AIID, names its machine method, its scales and its views, and points to where it can be browsed.
findings: THE DERIVATION RIGHT. AIID as the source and LLM pipelines as the method are the record's 'derived from' relation and intake. Checked 2026-10-29 against the MMRS meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-28 and the entity's own pages, re-read the same day.

THE COUNT, THREE WAYS. The tracker's page as read gives 'more than 1,400' in its description and 1,600 in its heading (the record); the card's summary gives 1,752; the Navigator card says 'more than 1300'. The composition gives none.
THE CAVEAT UNSAID. The page's own statement that patterns 'should be taken as indicative', with voluntary reporting and no validation study complete, is absent.
analysis: The tracker is composed as what it says it is, with its machine method named. Its count is unstable across MIT's own surfaces, and the composition avoids stating one; its caveat is dropped.
per_note: The MIT AI Risk Initiative and AIID named; Arcola AI on a card only; MIT's pages cited.
